reuse.why: Extends the tree's existing applyWeekendRule (already used by all three call sites) with the daily-skip case rather than adding a parallel helper.

duplication.why: The rule itself is in one place, but the 'scan 7 occurrences and drop skipped ones' idea is written twice with a bare magic 7 (getNextDate and getUpcomingDates), and getWeekendAdjustedDay re-checks skipWeekend that applyWeekendRule already checks.

placement.why: The daily-skip rule lives in shared/schedules.ts applyWeekendRule; frequency is carried in the schedule data built in rule-utils; server callers only consume it.

scope.why: Only weekend-handling paths, the rule data and focused tests are touched.

maintainability.why: A single rule with a documented null return is easy to own; the unnamed 7-occurrence window repeated in two files is a small wart.

disguised_duplication.where: The scan-window pattern in getNextDate and getUpcomingDates is visibly similar, not disguised.

one_place.where: applyWeekendRule in shared/schedules.ts decides skip vs move for getNextDate, getUpcomingDates (schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (schedule-template.ts).
